product.reading: Reading the canaries and their triggers.

templateHints.link: A URL to paste where only an intruder reads: a wiki page about passwords, a ticket, a bookmark.
templateHints.kubeconfig: A kubeconfig whose cluster is the canary URL. Any kubectl command with it calls the canary.
templateHints.env: A .env file with an admin API address and key. A script or person that tries the API calls the canary.
templateHints.html: A page called passwords.html with an invisible image. Opening it in a browser calls the canary.
templateHints.hostname: A DNS name to paste into a config. Any lookup of it, from anywhere, reaches deception.
templateHints.ssh-config: An SSH config with a bastion host whose name is the canary. Trying ssh bastion looks it up.
templateHints.aws-credentials: An AWS credentials file with a key of a user that may do nothing. CloudTrail shows each use.

overviewPage.description_one: {{count}} canary. Nobody has a reason to use one, so each use is worth a look.
overviewPage.description_other: {{count}} canaries. Nobody has a reason to use one, so each use is worth a look.
overviewPage.wasUsedFrom: {{name}} was used from {{source}} on {{when}}. Nobody has a reason to use it: treat it as a breach until shown otherwise.
overviewPage.nobodyHasAReason: Nobody has a reason to use a canary: treat each use as a breach until shown otherwise.
overviewPage.incidentsFailingDetail: Deception tries again for a day. The reason is on each trigger.
overviewPage.last30DaysDetail: Each day is red when a canary was used, tests left out.
overviewPage.noTriggersDetail: No canary has been used. That is how it should stay.

welcomePage.description: A canary is something only an attacker would use. When one is used, deception tells you at once.
welcomePage.step1: Make a canary from a template: a kubeconfig, a .env file, an SSH config, an AWS key and more.
welcomePage.step2: Plant its bait where an intruder looks: a home directory, a file share, a repository, a wiki.
welcomePage.step3: When it is used, deception keeps a trigger with where it came from, and opens an incident if it is linked to Incidents.
welcomePage.noDnsDetail: They need a zone delegated to deception. URL and AWS key canaries work without it. See Setup.

canariesPage.description: Tripwires that only an attacker would touch. Each has its own token, so a trigger names the copy that was used.
canariesPage.noneDetail: Make one with New canary, or change the filters.

newCanary.description: Pick what the bait looks like, then say where you will plant it, for the alert.
newCanary.noDnsDetail: Set DECEPTION_DNS_ZONE and delegate the zone to deception first. See Setup.
newCanary.name: Name
newCanary.locationHint: A path, share, repository or page, in your words.
newCanary.awsFirst: Make the key in AWS first
newCanary.awsFirstDetail: Create an IAM user that may do nothing and a key for it, then send its CloudTrail events to deception. The commands are under

plant.link: Paste the link where only an intruder would read it. Opening it calls the canary.
plant.kubeconfig: Save it as ~/.kube/config, or next to other kubeconfigs, on the host you named.
plant.env: Save it as .env where a script would keep its settings.
plant.html: Put the page on the share. Opening it in a browser calls the canary.
plant.hostname: Paste the name where a host name belongs, such as a database URL in a config.
plant.ssh-config: Save it as ~/.ssh/config, or add it to the one there.
plant.aws-credentials: Save it as ~/.aws/credentials on the host you named. The secret is kept sealed; you can show the bait again.

canaryDialog.enabledDetail: A turned-off canary keeps nothing when it is used. Its bait stays the same.
canaryDialog.deleteDetail: Its triggers are deleted with it, and a use afterwards leaves nothing. Remove the bait from where it is planted too.

triggersPage.description: Every use of a canary. Uses from the same address within 15 minutes are one trigger.

triggerPage.notFoundDetail: It may have been deleted with its canary, or after the retention.
triggerPage.treatAsBreach: Treat this as a breach until shown otherwise
triggerPage.treatAsBreachDetail: Nobody has a reason to use a canary. Find how the bait was reached: who signed in to the host, and what read the file.
triggerPage.incidentError: The incident could not be opened
triggerPage.dnsSource: For a DNS canary this is the last resolver that asked, not the person.
triggerPage.decideDetail: A breach stays one. A test needs a reason, such as who ran it; it is noted on the incident.

decided.confirmed: Marked as a breach by {{who}} on {{when}}
decided.test: Marked as a test by {{who}} on {{when}}

triggerPage.timelineDetail: The first 100 uses of this trigger.

setupPage.description: Where canaries call home, and what each kind needs.
setupPage.urlsDetail: They call /c/<token> at this address. Any path answers the same transparent image, so nothing tells the caller it found a canary.
setupPage.sameAddress: Canaries call the address people open deception at, which names the product. Set DECEPTION_CANARY_URL to another name, such as cdn.example.com, behind the same proxy.
setupPage.dnsOff: Off. Set DECEPTION_DNS_ZONE and delegate the zone to deception.
setupPage.awsDetail: A key of a user that may do nothing. Deception finds its use in CloudTrail events you send.
setupPage.incidentsOn: Each trigger opens an incident in Incidents.
setupPage.incidentsOff: Not linked. Set DECEPTION_INCIDENTS_TOKEN to an Incidents API token with the editor role, and each trigger opens an incident.

settingsPage.askAnAdmin: Ask an admin of this deception.

account.title: Account
account.description: Your profile, password, two-step verification and where you are signed in.

members.title: Members
members.description: Who can sign in to this deception, and with which role. Viewers see everything; editors also make canaries, see their bait and decide on triggers; admins also delete canaries, and manage members and tokens.

signin.title: Sign-in
signin.description: Identity providers people can sign in with, such as OpenAsy Identity, Keycloak or Microsoft Entra ID, and which of their groups give which role.

tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.description: For scripts and CI. Each token has one role and an expiry; the secret is shown once.
